lines.text: He sprays a whole can of Seafoam into a tired old Ford Ranger and look at that smoke.
The engine has 167000 miles and its lifters tick so loud it sounds like a diesel.
So he puts Seafoam in the tank and the oil and sprays the rest straight into the intake.
And the throttle plate is caked in black carbon that starts melting off as he sprays.
That smoke is the solvent burning off with some of the carbon it broke loose inside the cylinders.
beats: ai:black carbon flakes breaking off the top of an engine piston in slow motion macro

lines.text: Then the new oil comes out almost black after just three hours because the old sludge got dissolved and washed out.
beats: ai:thick black engine sludge dissolving into dark oil macro

lines.text: Then he adds Lucas oil stabilizer which is so thick it barely pours.
And thicker oil holds more pressure in worn lifters so the ticking almost disappears.
beats: ai:cutaway of an engine lifter filling with golden oil under pressure

lines.text: But it's one old truck and no lab test so it's a hopeful fix and not a miracle.
So would you trust Seafoam on your engine?
